---
title: "Blueprint: architecture and data models"
description: "Use Blueprint to see what your app is made of, what it connects to and which identity each connection uses, plus its Rayfin data model and the Fabric data it reads."
---

Use **Blueprint** to see how your app is put together. The **Architecture** view shows what the app is made of, what it connects to, and which identity each connection uses. The **Data model** view shows the Rayfin data model, and the **Fabric data** view shows the Fabric data the app connects to: its semantic models, and the tables of its SQL databases, warehouses and lakehouses.

![The Architecture view of the Contoso Expenses sample app. People on the left connect to the app in the middle, which lists its app identity and its pieces: Website, Sign-in, Database, File storage, Connectors, Functions and Secrets. Lines run from the Connectors and Functions ports to the semantic models, warehouse, Azure services and web API on the right, grouped by where they live.](/screenshots/blueprint.webp)

## Open Blueprint

1. Open a project.
2. Select **Blueprint** in the project tabs.
3. Choose **Architecture**, **Data model** or **Fabric data**. **Fabric data** appears when the app connects to a semantic model, SQL database, warehouse or lakehouse.

Fabricator remembers the view you chose for the project.

## Read the architecture

The **Architecture** view reads the app's `rayfin/rayfin.yml`, `fabric.yaml`, data model and function code. From left to right it shows:

- **People**, the people who use the app, and how they sign in.
- The app, named with the workspace it's in. When any connection uses the app identity, **App identity** names whose credentials it uses. Below are the app's pieces: **Website**, **Sign-in**, **Database**, **File storage**, **Connectors**, **Functions** and **Secrets**, as the app has them.
- What the app connects to, grouped by where it lives: each Fabric workspace by name, with its capacity and region when Fabric returns them, then **Microsoft Fabric**, **Azure** and **Web APIs**.

A piece that connects to something outside the app lists how those connections sign in, with a count. Lines run from there to each source. Hover or select a piece, a source or one of those rows to highlight the connections it's part of.

Use **Search the app and its connections** to highlight matching pieces and sources. The toolbar also has **Open the app** and **Open in Fabric** once the app is deployed, plus zoom and fit-to-view.

If the app connects to nothing outside, the view says **No outside data yet** and offers **Connect data with Copilot**. If `rayfin/rayfin.yml` can't be read, it says "Couldn’t draw the app" and offers **Open rayfin.yml**.

## Which identity a connection uses

| Label | What it means | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Uses user’s identity** | Delegated access. The connection runs as the signed-in person, so Fabric checks their own permissions and each person sees only what they can access. | Connectors with `auth.type: delegated`, and semantic models in `fabric.yaml` |
| **Uses app identity** | Application access. The connection runs as the app identity, so everyone sees the same data. | Connectors with `auth.type: application`, and function connections through `ctx.Tokens` |
| **Uses a key** | The function sends its own key or token. Anyone who has the key has the same access. | Web APIs that functions call directly |

The app's own database always uses the user's identity, and each table's access rules decide which rows a person can see. Learn more in the [Rayfin delegated access docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/auth/delegated-access).

## Whose credentials the app identity uses

The app identity is the owner of the app's Fabric item:

- For your own apps, it's the Fabric account that first deployed the app. Fabricator shows the account it deploys with. Before the first deploy, it shows "Whoever deploys it first".
- For a team app, it's the team workspace's deploy identity. Previews are owned by the preview identity when the team has a separate one.

Select **App identity** to see which sources the app identity needs access to, and select **Ask Copilot what to grant** to ask which role to give it on each one.

## When the website's pages load

The **Website** piece shows when people can load the app's pages, set by `assetAccess` in `rayfin/rayfin.yml`:

- **Pages load after sign-in** (`protected`): the page files load only for people signed in to Fabric.
- **Pages load before sign-in** (`public`): anyone with the link can download the page files, the app's HTML, JavaScript and CSS. The app's data still needs sign-in, and its access rules still apply.
- **Page access not set**: choose `protected` or `public` before deploying.

## How people sign in

The **Sign-in** piece shows how people sign in to the app. **Microsoft Entra ID, through Fabric** means the app uses Fabric brokered auth, which Rayfin's docs also call Fabric SSO:

- People sign in with the Microsoft Entra account they already use for Fabric.
- Sign-in is part of the app, so there's no identity provider to run.
- The app needs no app registration of its own in Microsoft Entra ID, so there's nothing for a tenant admin to approve.

Select **Sign-in** to see its **Provider**, whether it accepts **Entra tokens from other apps**, and its **Sign-in addresses**. If the piece says **Off**, the app can't tell people apart. Learn more in the [Rayfin auth docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/auth).

## Secrets

The **Secrets** piece lists the secrets the app's functions use: the ones declared in `rayfin/rayfin.yml` and the ones its code reads. Select it to see what each secret is for, which functions read it, and whether the deployed app has a value for it: **Set**, **No value** or **Not in rayfin.yml**. Values are never shown.

Fabricator flags a secret that functions read with `ctx.Secrets` but that `rayfin/rayfin.yml` doesn't declare, which is a TypeScript error, and reads that use the deprecated `ctx.getSecret()`.

Select **Manage secrets** to add or change values in **Code → Secrets**. If keys are written into the functions' code, select **Move keys into secrets** to ask Copilot to move them. See [Secrets](/docs/build/secrets).

## Details and actions

Select any card to open its details: what it is, the settings it comes from, its IDs, and what it connects to. Press Esc or select the empty canvas to close them.

Depending on what you select, the details can include:

- **Use user’s identity** or **Use app identity**, to ask Copilot to change a connector's `auth.type`.
- **Fix with Copilot**, when a connector's `auth.type` or the functions' `services.functions.auth.type` would stop the app from deploying.
- **Use app identity** on a web API that Rayfin can also reach with the app identity, so the functions don't need a key for it.
- **View the model**, which opens a semantic model in the **Fabric data** view.
- **View the tables**, which opens a SQL database, warehouse or lakehouse in the **Fabric data** view.
- **Open in Fabric**, which opens a source or its workspace in the Fabric portal.
- **Harden access** and **Open the data model** on **Database**.

These actions send a prompt to the Build chat. Fabricator doesn't deploy from them directly; the normal chat turn and redeploy apply.

## Read the data model diagram

The **Data model** view parses the Rayfin schema and draws an entity-relationship diagram. Each entity card shows:

- The entity name.
- Each field and its type: `uuid`, `text`, `email`, `int`, `decimal`, `bool`, `date`, or `enum` for a `@set()` field. A relationship field shows the entity it points to, such as `Category`, with `[]` after it when it holds many, such as `Task[]`.
- A key on the primary key, and a link on a field that references another entity.
- A diamond before each field name: filled for a required field, hollow for an optional field and for the primary key, and in the accent color for a unique field. Hover over it to see **Required** or **Optional**.
- Access grants, including role names and whether a grant has a row-level **policy**.
- An access dot. The legend labels access as **Row-scoped**, **Any signed-in** or **Public**.

Relationships appear as lines between entity cards, and the header counts the entities and relationships, such as **4 entities · 3 relationships**. Hover an entity to highlight its related entities.

![The Data model view showing the Expense entity as a card with its fields and types, an authenticated access tag with a policy, and Open and Focus buttons.](/screenshots/model.webp)

![The Data model view with four entities: Expense, whose report field links to Report, whose expenses field shows Expense with brackets, and an ExpenseTag join entity linked to both Expense and Tag. The header reads 4 entities · 3 relationships.](/screenshots/model-relations.webp)

Learn the Rayfin modeling concepts in the [Rayfin data modeling docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/data/modeling).

## Navigate and search the diagram

Use the toolbar to:

- Search with **Search entities & fields**.
- **Collapse** or **Expand** all entities.
- Zoom in or out.
- Fit the diagram to view.
- Reset the layout.

You can drag entity cards to rearrange the diagram. Fabricator stores the layout in the app for that project.

Each entity card also has:

- **Open**, which opens the entity source file in **Code**.
- **Focus**, which shows that entity and its neighbors. Use **Unfocus** to return to the full diagram.

## Harden loose access

Fabricator flags loose access on entities that are public, authenticated-only, default or mixed. Those cards show **Harden**.

![The Data model view with four entities. Expense, ExpenseTag and Tag have green access dots and an authenticated grant with a policy. Report has an amber dot, says no explicit roles, and offers Harden beside Open and Focus.](/screenshots/model-access.webp)

Select **Harden** to send a ready prompt to Copilot asking it to tighten the entity's access control with Rayfin decorators and row-level policy. Fabricator does not deploy from that prompt directly; the normal chat turn and redeploy flow applies.

```prompt title="Add row-level access"
Restrict the Customer and Order entities so each signed-in user only sees rows they own. Use Rayfin role or authenticated decorators with row-level policies, and keep the app building.
```

Learn more in the [Rayfin permissions docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/data/permissions).

## Add a data model

The data model is where the app keeps its entities. New projects keep it in `packages/data/src/`, registered in `packages/data/src/index.ts`. Apps that keep everything in one package use `rayfin/data/`, registered in `rayfin/data/schema.ts`. Fabricator reads `rayfin/rayfin.yml` to find it.

If the app has no schema file yet, the **Data model** view says **No data model yet** and offers **Add a data model with Copilot**. If the schema file exists but lists no entities, as in a new project, it says **Your schema has no entities** and offers **Add an entity with Copilot**.

Those actions stage a prompt in the Build chat composer. New projects start without a database, so the prompt also asks Copilot to turn on the data service.

```prompt title="Add an entity and relationship"
Add Project and Task entities. A project has many tasks. Tasks have a title, due date, status and owner. Restrict access so users only see their own projects and tasks.
```

## View the Fabric data the app connects to

The **Fabric data** view draws each source the app reads from Microsoft Fabric: its semantic models, and the tables of its SQL databases, warehouses and lakehouses. When the app connects to more than one, choose a source above the diagram. Each one shows its name and its kind, such as **Warehouse**.

## View a semantic model

When the app uses semantic models, from `fabric.yaml` or a semantic model connector, the **Fabric data** view reads them live from Fabric and draws a diagram of:

- Tables.
- Columns and data types.
- Measures. Select a measure to show its DAX.
- Relationships, including one-to-many markers, inactive relationships and cross-filter direction.
- Hidden tables or columns.
- Storage mode and descriptions when Fabric returns them.

Use **Search tables, columns & measures**, **Collapse** or **Expand**, focus controls, zoom, fit-to-view and **Refresh from Fabric** to work with the diagram.

Learn about Rayfin semantic model connectors in the [Rayfin semantic models docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/connectors/semantic-models).

## View the tables of a SQL database, warehouse or lakehouse

For a SQL database, warehouse or lakehouse connector, the **Fabric data** view draws the source's tables from the app's files, so it doesn't need to sign in to Fabric. Each table card shows:

- Each column and its SQL type, such as `nvarchar(30)` or `decimal(8,2)`.
- A key on each primary key column, and a link on each foreign key column.
- A diamond before each column name: filled for a required column, hollow for a column that can be empty. Hover over a column to see its type, the column it references, and whether the database fills it in.
- The app's entity for the table. Select it to open the entity file in **Code**. A table the app doesn't use says **Not used by the app**.

Foreign keys appear as lines between the tables, with one and many markers. The header counts the tables and relationships, and says when Rayfin discovered the tables.

When the app uses some of the source's tables, the view starts on **Used by the app**, the tables the app has an entity for. Select **All tables** to see every table Rayfin discovered. Use **Search tables & columns**, **Collapse** or **Expand**, focus controls, zoom and fit-to-view to work with the diagram, and **Open metadata.json** to open the discovered tables as a file.

Rayfin discovers a source's tables when the connector is added, and keeps them in `rayfin/connectors/<name>/metadata.json`. Copilot then writes an entity file for each table the app needs. Lakehouses usually don't report keys or relationships, so their tables show neither.

- If the app doesn't use any of the source's tables yet, the view says "The app doesn’t use these tables yet." and offers **Use them with Copilot**.
- If `metadata.json` is missing, the view draws only the tables the app's entity files describe, and offers **Discover the tables with Copilot**.
- If there's nothing to draw, the view says "No tables to draw yet" and offers **Discover the tables with Copilot**.

These actions stage a prompt in the Build chat composer. Learn how Copilot turns the discovered tables into entities in the [Rayfin entity generation docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/connectors/entity-generation).

## Connect Fabric data

Your app can read data that's already in Microsoft Fabric through Rayfin connectors: semantic
models, warehouses, SQL databases, and lakehouses, which apps read through their SQL analytics
endpoint and can't change. You pick the data; Copilot connects it.

1. In the Build chat composer, select **+** (**Add images, files or data**), then
   **Fabric data**.
2. Choose a kind of data, such as **Warehouse**, or **Browse all Fabric data…**.
3. In **Add Fabric data**, choose a workspace. **Recent** lists the workspaces your apps
   deploy to and the ones you connected data from, newest first. Below it are all the other
   workspaces you can open.
4. Tick the data you want. You can pick from several workspaces before you add it.
5. Select **Add to chat**. The data waits in the message box as chips, one for each item,
   showing its name and workspace.
6. Say what to build with it, such as "Chart spending by category", or just press **Enter**
   to connect it. Fabricator tells Copilot how to connect the data when you send, so you
   don't have to.

![Add Fabric data: recent workspaces first, the Finance analytics workspace open with its semantic models, warehouse, SQL database and lakehouses, three already connected and two picked](/screenshots/connect-data.webp)

![The message box with two Fabric data chips, Ledger and Raw transactions from Finance analytics, above the placeholder "Say what to build with this data, or just press Enter to connect it"](/screenshots/data-chips.webp)

To change the data before you send, select a chip to reopen **Add Fabric data**, or select
its **×** to remove it. The chips stay on your message in the chat, so you can see what
each request connected.

Copilot adds each one with `rayfin connector add` and wires it into the app. Data the app
already connects to is marked **Connected**. The dialog starts in the workspace this app
deploys to, when it has one, but the app doesn't need to be deployed to connect data.

Fabricator doesn't offer KQL databases: Rayfin 1.36 can't add new KQL database connectors.
Learn more in the [Rayfin connectors docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/connectors).

## Sign in and retry

Listing your workspaces and their data uses Fabric authentication. If Fabricator can't list
them silently, the dialog says: "Sign in to Fabric to see your workspaces and their data."
Select **Sign in & retry**.

Reading a semantic model schema can also require sign-in:

- **Sign in to Fabric** appears when the Fabric session is missing.
- **Sign in to Azure** appears when the schema query needs an Azure CLI session.

If the schema cannot be read, the **Fabric data** view shows "Couldn’t read the semantic model" and offers **Try again**. You can still choose the app's other sources above the message. SQL databases, warehouses and lakehouses don't need sign-in, because Fabricator reads their tables from the app's files. For Fabric deployment and authentication recovery, see [Deploy troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/deploy).
